name: Tuomo Suntola
summary: Finnish Doctor of Science in Technology, inventor of atomic layer epitaxy (ALE/ALD) and the Humicap humidity sensor, founder of Microchemistry Ltd.

name: Riikka L. Puurunen
summary: ALD researcher at VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland and author of the ALE history essay.

name: Thor Stubb
summary: Professor heading the Electron Physics laboratory at Helsinki University of Technology; Suntola's doctoral-era supervisor.

name: Tapio Wiik
summary: Suntola's colleague at the VTT Semiconductor Laboratory who made the humidity sensing pre-study.

name: Jorma Antson
summary: Suntola's co-worker on the Humicap humidity sensor, co-inventor on the first ALE patent, later working on ion-selective sensors.

name: Sven Lindfors
summary: Suntola's closest co-worker in ALE reactor design, co-inventor on the second ALE patent, co-founder of Picosun Oy.

name: Arto Pakkala
summary: ALE-EL team member, co-inventor on the second ALE patent, operator of early ALE-EL prototype reactors.

name: Antti Piippo
summary: Business-oriented manager of Lohja's Display Electronics division, later owner of Elcoteq.

name: Ralf Graeffe
summary: Lohja EL team member who inspected the Helsinki-Vantaa airport test assembly.

name: Ahti Aintila
summary: Led development of EL driving circuitry and manufacturing technology at Lohja; founder of Picopack Oy.

name: Ulf Ström
summary: Managing director of Finlux Inc., responsible for marketing ALE-EL panels in the USA.

name: Tapio Alvesalo
summary: Head of Neste's venture team NAPS who proposed applying ALE to thin film solar panels.

name: Jaakko Hyvärinen
summary: Microchemistry PV researcher who built the flash solar simulator and founded Endeas Oy.

name: Aimo Rautiainen
summary: One of the first chemists in the Microchemistry team, working on ALE catalysts.

name: Eeva-Liisa Lakomaa
summary: One of the first chemists in the Microchemistry team, working on ALE catalysts.

name: Marina Lindblad
summary: Microchemistry researcher whose doctoral thesis completed the quantum chemical analysis of ZnS ALE growth.

name: Suvi Haukka
summary: Microchemistry researcher who produced a doctoral dissertation on ALE catalysts.

name: Arla Kytökivi
summary: Microchemistry researcher who produced a doctoral dissertation on ALE catalysts.

name: Matti Ervasti
summary: Business-oriented managing director who succeeded Suntola at Microchemistry Ltd.

name: Heli Vaara
summary: Assistant to Suntola at Microchemistry, present at the MRS 1994 ALE booth.

name: Kustaa Poutiainen
summary: Co-founder of Picosun Oy with Sven Lindfors.

name: Pekka Soininen
summary: Started the ALE reactor activity at Beneq Oy.

name: Jun-ichi Nishizawa
summary: Japanese professor (Semiconductor Laboratory, Sendai) who pursued ALE growth of GaAs under the name Molecular Layer Epitaxy.

name: Salah Bedair
summary: North Carolina State University professor who demonstrated ALE of GaAs in a rotating-disk CVD system.

name: DenBaars
summary: University of Southern California professor whose group demonstrated ALD of GaAs in an atmospheric MOCVD system.

name: Lauri Niinistö
summary: Professor of inorganic and analytical chemistry at HUT, ALE chemistry consultant to Suntola and chair of the ALE-1 symposium.

name: Markku Leskelä
summary: Professor heading ALD activities at the University of Helsinki Laboratory of Inorganic Chemistry.

name: Mikko Ritala
summary: Professor heading ALD activities at the University of Helsinki Laboratory of Inorganic Chemistry.

name: Tapani Pakkanen
summary: University of Joensuu professor who collaborated on quantum chemical analysis of ZnS ALE growth.

name: M. Ahonen
summary: Graduate student at Tampere University of Technology who took up ALE of group III-V semiconductors.

name: Markus Pessa
summary: Professor of physics at Tampere University of Technology directing III-V MBE research leading to GaAs laser technology.

name: Victor Drozd
summary: Leningrad/St. Petersburg researcher of molecular layering who invited Suntola to meet Aleskovskii.

name: V. B. Aleskovskii
summary: Soviet professor at the University of Leningrad who co-originated the molecular layering technique.

name: S. I. Kol'tsov
summary: Soviet professor who co-originated the molecular layering technique with Aleskovskii.

name: Stanley Myers
summary: President & CEO of SEMI (USA) who handed the European SEMI Award to Suntola.

name: Tampere
summary: City in Finland, Suntola's birthplace and home of Tampere University of Technology.

name: Turku
summary: City in Finland where Suntola went to school.

name: Espoo
summary: City in Finland hosting Instrumentarium's Tapiola lab, HUT/VTT in Otaniemi, and the Olarinluoma EL plant.

name: Olarinluoma EL plant
summary: Cleanroom EL production facility in Espoo, Olarinluoma, built by Lohja and later operated by Planar and Beneq.

name: Kunnarla plant
summary: Lohja Oy plant in the town of Lohja where TF-EL pilot production took place.

name: Helsinki
summary: Capital of Finland.

name: Helsinki-Vantaa airport
summary: Airport where the first large ALE-EL information boards were installed.

name: Moscow
summary: Soviet capital, site of the ALE patent hearing.

name: Leningrad
summary: Soviet city, home of the University of Leningrad and the molecular layering group.

name: San Diego
summary: City in California, site of the 1980 SID conference and ICVGE-5.

name: Kobe
summary: City in Japan, site of the 16th Conference on Solid State Devices and Materials.

name: Boston
summary: City in Massachusetts, site of the MRS 1994 Fall Meeting.

name: New York
summary: US city where Lohja met an American semiconductor manufacturer.

name: Munich
summary: German city hosting the Munich Electronics Show 2004.

name: Phoenix, Arizona
summary: Location of the ASM plant to which ALE reactor manufacturing was moved.

name: France
summary: Country where ALE-EL was licensed and where NAPS acquired an a-Si solar panel factory.

name: Finland
summary: Country where ALE was invented and commercialized.

name: Soviet Union
summary: Country where molecular layering was developed and where the ALE patent was granted.

name: Japan
summary: Country with prominent group III-V ALE research in the mid-1980s.

name: United States
summary: Country of Planar Inc. and major early ALE-EL distribution.

name: Helsinki University of Technology
summary: Finnish technical university (now Aalto University) where Suntola studied and obtained his doctorate.

name: VTT Semiconductor Laboratory
summary: VTT laboratory integrated with Stubb's Electron Physics laboratory at HUT; Suntola's employer for the humidity sensor work.

name: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland
summary: Finnish national technical research centre.

name: Vaisala Oy
summary: Finnish meteorological instrumentation company that commissioned and commercialized the Humicap humidity sensor.

name: Instrumentarium Oy
summary: Finnish medical instrumentation trading house that hosted Suntola's research group where ALE was invented.

name: Datex Oy
summary: Small technology company established by Instrumentarium, maker of a dialysis bed-scale and CO2/CO anesthesia meter.

name: INSKO
summary: Finnish engineering training organization for which Suntola lectured on display technologies.

name: Lohja Oy
summary: Finnish building material company that acquired the ALE-EL project and became the world's third EL display manufacturer.

name: Planar Inc.
summary: US EL display manufacturer that acquired Lohja's EL business.

name: Planar International
summary: Finnish EL activity operated as a subsidiary of US Planar.

name: Beneq Oy
summary: Finnish company producing ALE-EL panels and ALD reactors.

name: Picopack Oy
summary: Company founded by Ahti Aintila producing smart cards using TAB technology.

name: Elcoteq Oy
summary: Contract electronics manufacturer spun out of Lohja's microelectronics division, supplier to Nokia.

name: Nokia
summary: Finnish mobile phone maker for which Elcoteq was a contract manufacturer.

name: Aspo Oy
summary: Finnish company from which Antti Piippo was recruited to Lohja.

name: Finlux Inc.
summary: Company responsible for marketing ALE-EL panels in the USA.

name: Sharp
summary: Japanese EL display manufacturer, one of the first in the world.

name: Neste Oy
summary: Finnish national oil company, parent of NAPS and Microchemistry Ltd.

name: Neste Advanced Power Systems
summary: Neste's corporate venture unit for renewable energy solutions.

name: Microchemistry Ltd.
summary: Neste subsidiary founded by Suntola for ALE-based solar panels and catalysts, later the first commercial ALE reactor vendor.

name: Fortum Oyj
summary: Finnish energy company formed by the fusion of Neste and IVO.

name: IVO
summary: Finnish state electric utility company merged with Neste to form Fortum.

name: Fortum Foundation
summary: Foundation of Fortum for which Suntola served as attorney.

name: World Energy Council
summary: International energy organization of which Suntola was a member.

name: ASM
summary: Dutch semiconductor equipment company that acquired Microchemistry Ltd.

name: ASM Microchemistry
summary: ASM's Finnish ALE unit continuing Microchemistry's activity, focused on ALE research with the University of Helsinki.

name: Picosun Oy
summary: Finnish ALD reactor company founded by Sven Lindfors and Kustaa Poutiainen.

name: Endeas Oy
summary: Company founded by Jaakko Hyvärinen to produce Quicksun solar simulators.

name: University of Helsinki
aliases: Laboratory of Inorganic Chemistry, University of Helsinki
summary: Finnish university whose Laboratory of Inorganic Chemistry hosts the Finnish Centre of Excellence in ALD.

name: Finnish Centre of Excellence in Atomic Layer Deposition
summary: Academy of Finland Centre of Excellence in ALD headed by Leskelä and Ritala.

name: University of Joensuu
summary: Finnish university where Tapani Pakkanen carried out quantum chemical ALE studies.

name: Tampere University of Technology
summary: Finnish technical university where Suntola was docent and encouraged III-V ALE research.

name: University of Leningrad
summary: Soviet university home to Aleskovskii's molecular layering group.

name: North Carolina State University
summary: US university where Bedair's group demonstrated ALE of GaAs.

name: University of Southern California
summary: Los Angeles university where DenBaars's group demonstrated ALD of GaAs by MOCVD.

name: Nippon Electric Company
summary: Japanese company that demonstrated an InGaP-GaAs-InGaP superlattice using ALE cycles.

name: Society for Information Display
summary: Display technology society whose 1980 conference hosted the first public ALE-EL disclosure.

name: Materials Research Society
summary: Materials science society whose 1994 Fall Meeting hosted Suntola's ALE talk and booth.

name: SEMI
summary: Semiconductor equipment and materials industry association that gave Suntola the European SEMI Award.

name: CGE
summary: Big French state-owned company that sought an ALE-EL license from Lohja.

name: Sintra Alcatel
summary: French state-owned company that received the ALE-EL license in place of CGE.

name: Physics Foundations Society
summary: Espoo-based society chaired by Suntola, publisher of his books on physics foundations.

name: Finnish Society for Natural Philosophy
summary: Society where Suntola serves as board member and lecturer.

name: Atomic layer epitaxy (ALE)
summary: Thin film growth technique based on repeated, separate, saturating gas-solid surface reactions; later renamed atomic layer deposition.

name: Molecular layering
summary: Soviet thin-film build-up technique based on saturated surface reactions, an independent discovery of the ALD principle.

name: Molecular Layer Epitaxy (MLE)
summary: Nishizawa's name for his ALE-type GaAs growth, later admitted to be the same technique as ALE.

name: First ALE patent (FIN 52359 / US 4,058,430)
summary: International patent on ALE as a method for growing compound thin films from elemental reactants, granted in over twenty countries.

name: Second ALE patent (FIN 57975 / US 4,413,022)
summary: International patent protecting the inert gas ALE reactor, chloride processes, and ALE dielectric layers for EL displays.

name: Humicap humidity sensor
summary: Capacitive thin polymer film humidity sensor commercialized by Vaisala, world market leader in humidity measurement.

name: Humidity sensor patent (US 4,164,868)
summary: Suntola's international patent underlying the Humicap sensor.

name: LCD color display patent (US 4,907,862)
aliases: Method for generating electronically controllable color elements and color display based on the method
summary: Suntola's patent on a sequential color concept for liquid crystal displays, intended as a fallback for full-color displays.

name: First ALE reactor (rotating carousel)
summary: Hybrid ALE-PVD high-vacuum reactor built in a 12-inch T-piece with a rotating substrate carousel and elemental Zn and S sources.

name: Inert gas ALE reactor
summary: Batch-type ALE reactor with inert gas valving enabling uninterrupted processing of the full EL dielectric/ZnS(Mn)/dielectric stack.

name: F-120 reactor
summary: Compact fast-cycling ALE research reactor designed at Microchemistry; the first commercial ALD reactor.

name: F-450 reactor
summary: Microchemistry ALE reactor for silicon wafers and glass substrates up to 450 mm x 450 mm.

name: F-1000 reactor
summary: Large Microchemistry ALD reactor for big batches of 500 mm x 500 mm substrates.

name: Quicksun solar simulator
summary: Single-xenon-flash I-V solar simulator developed by Jaakko Hyvärinen and sold by Endeas Oy.

name: ALE-EL thin film electroluminescent display
summary: Thin film EL display with ALE-grown dielectric/ZnS(Mn)/dielectric stack, noted for high contrast and reliability.

name: Master's thesis on Schottky diodes
summary: Suntola's HUT diplomityö on metal-semiconductor diodes for radar detectors at microwave frequencies.

name: Licentiate's thesis on chalcogenide switching
aliases: On the mechanism of switching effect in chalcogenide thin films
summary: Suntola's licentiate thesis on the switching mechanism in amorphous chalcogenide thin films, published in Solid State Electronics.

name: Doctoral thesis: Electrical Conduction and Switching in Chalcogenide Thin Films
summary: Suntola's HUT doctoral thesis explaining Ovonic switching by current filament heating above 700 °C.

name: Atomic layer epitaxy for producing EL thin films (SID 1980)
summary: First public disclosure of ALE-EL displays, SID International Symposium Digest of Technical Papers.

name: 1980 SID Outstanding Paper Award
summary: Award given to Suntola, Antson, Lindfors and Pakkala for the EL work.

name: European SEMI Award 2004
summary: Award honoring the pioneer in atomic layer deposition techniques that paved the way for nanoscale semiconductor devices.

name: Atomic layer epitaxy review (Mater. Sci. Reports 1989)
summary: Suntola's 1989 review paper mapping known laboratories working on ALE.

name: The Dynamic Universe – toward a unified picture of physical reality
summary: Suntola's book presenting a holistic picture of physical reality, published by Physics Foundations Society.

name: The Short History of Science – or the long path to the union of metaphysics and empiricism
summary: Suntola's book linking his philosophical considerations to the historical development of science.

name: Some characteristics of molecular layering reactions (1965)
summary: Aleskovskii and Kol'tsov's Russian-language conference abstract on molecular layering, Goskhimizdat, Leningrad.
